webglEntryPoint.name: texElementImage2D
webglEntryPoint.signature: current 3-arg (target, internalformat, element) - three.js calls this its "Chrome 150+" branch
webglEntryPoint.verdict: texElementImage2D is the name that shipped here, with the current 3-arg (target, internalformat, element) signature.

geometryApi.name: getElementTransform
geometryApi.verdict: This browser ships the OLDER generation: getElementTransform(element, screenSpaceTransform) exists, updateElementGeometry does not. The panel is positioned by writing the returned matrix to element.style.transform, so hit-testing, focus, selection and a11y geometry come from a genuinely transformed DOM element rather than from a canvas-side geometry call.

groups.title: HTMLCanvasElement.prototype
groups.subtitle: The five primitives, as declared in the README IDL block.

results.name: requestPaint
results.note: The gate. three.js HTMLTexture.js tests exactly this, as `'requestPaint' in parent`. If this is false nothing else matters.

results.name: onpaint
results.note: The `paint` event handler. Fires after the Paint step; DOM changes made inside it land on the NEXT frame.

results.name: layoutSubtree
results.note: README IDL: `[CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean layoutSubtree`. Content attribute is lowercase `layoutsubtree`.

results.name: captureElementImage
results.note: Takes an `ElementImage` snapshot that can be transferred to a worker and drawn to an OffscreenCanvas.

results.name: updateElementGeometry
results.note: MANDATORY for 3D contexts. Supplies `canvasTransform`, which is what adds a11y GEOMETRY and inserts the element into the canvas hit-test list. 2D gets it free from drawElementImage; WebGL does not.

results.name: clearElementGeometry
results.note: Clears the hit-test entry and canvas transform set by updateElementGeometry.

results.name: getCanvasTransform
results.note: README IDL spelling. Returns the element's border-box -> canvas DOMMatrix.

results.name: getElementTransform
results.note: The OTHER half of the same rename - the spelling used by the WebGPU demo and by published guidance. Probed so we learn which one shipped.

results.name: onelementgeometryupdate
results.note: Fires when OffscreenCanvas-originated geometry updates have been applied on the main thread.

groups.title: layoutsubtree reflection
groups.subtitle: Declared is not the same as reflecting. Both directions are checked on a real <canvas>.

results.name: 'layoutSubtree' in HTMLCanvasElement.prototype
results.note: The IDL attribute is declared. Necessary, not sufficient.

results.name: canvas.layoutSubtree = true  ->  [layoutsubtree]
results.note: Property reflects out to the content attribute.

results.name: [layoutsubtree]  ->  canvas.layoutSubtree
results.note: Content attribute reflects back to the property. three.js writes the ATTRIBUTE, so this direction is the one it depends on.

groups.title: WebGL2 entry point
groups.subtitle: Mid-rename. Both candidate spellings are probed by name.

results.name: texElementSubImage2D
results.note: The CURRENT README IDL name (partial interface WebGLRenderingContext). Not called by three.js and not called by the spec repo's own demo - the IDL is ahead of the implementation.

results.name: texElementImage2D
results.note: The name that Examples/webGL.html and three.js WebGLTextures.js actually call. If exactly one of these two exists, this is the one that shipped.

groups.title: CanvasRenderingContext2D
groups.subtitle: Not our path, but a useful corroboration that the flag is on.

results.name: drawElementImage
results.note: The 2D draw path. Not used by this product - the panel goes into a WebGL texture - but its presence corroborates that the flag is on rather than a single member being polyfilled.

groups.title: Global interfaces
groups.subtitle: Which interfaces the API generation brought with it.

results.name: ElementImage
results.note: The transferable snapshot handle returned by captureElementImage.

results.name: PaintEvent
results.note: README IDL declares `interface PaintEvent : Event` with a `changedElements` list. three.js reads `event.changedElements` in its paint handler, so the data is delivered even where the constructor is not exposed.

results.name: ElementGeometryUpdateEvent
results.note: Only meaningful alongside updateElementGeometry. Its absence corroborates which generation of the API shipped.

tierReason: 'requestPaint' in HTMLCanvasElement.prototype is true, so html-in-canvas is exposed and the panel's DOM pixels can reach the screen mesh through three.js HTMLTexture. This is the main path.
